title: Hedge regret bound against an adaptive adversary
statement:
Fix $N \ge 1$ experts, a horizon of $T$ rounds, and a learning rate $\eta > 0$. Let the Hedge algorithm with rate $\eta$ — the learner policy whose round-$t$ distribution is the exponential-weights distribution $p_t(i) \propto \exp(-\eta L_t(i))$ built from the past realized cumulative losses — play against an arbitrary adaptive adversary, whose loss vectors have every coordinate in $[0,1]$ and may depend on the full history of losses and on the learner's current distribution. Let $\ell$ be the loss sequence realized over the $T$ rounds of this interaction. Then the regret of Hedge, its cumulative expected loss minus the least cumulative loss $L^* = \min_{i} L_T(i)$ of any single expert in hindsight, satisfies
\[
  R_T(\eta) \;\le\; \frac{\log N}{\eta} + \frac{\eta\, T}{8}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: arbitrary adaptive adversary with loss coordinates in [0,1]
losses realized by running Hedge against the adversary
